transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-06-30
Start: 14:00 PDT
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE); Ethan Ross (Redwood SE); Liam O'Connor (Security Lead, Zenith); Priya Shah (Platform Eng, Zenith); Daniel Weiss (Head of Compliance, Zenith)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be incomplete): Quick run-through of audit capture and export capabilities, discussion of KMS and key residency, retention windows and legal hold. Next: share artifacts + sample schemas, schedule POC planning.

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Maya (Redwood): Hi everyone, thanks for joining — we, uh, really appreciate you carving time today. Quick roll call?
[00:08] Liam (Zenith): Hey, Liam here. Priya's on. Daniel's on as well.
[00:12] Priya (Zenith): Priya Shaah — sorry, Shah — here.
[00:15] Daniel (Zenith): Daniel Weiss, compliance.
[00:18] Maya: Awesome. I'll kick us off — high level goal for today is to confirm what admin and audit telemetry Redwood captures, what we can export, retention and any data residency constraints, and then touch on KMS/hsm options for key residency. Ethan will run through the technical bits.
[00:34] Ethan (Redwood): Cool. So start with what we capture. At a top level: we track all control-plane admin events — user creates/deletes, RBAC changes, API key ops, grant/revoke sessions, SSO logins, failed auths, role assumption, model pinning, and deployment rollouts. We also record per-request metadata for inference calls that are considered admin-scope, e.g., console admin previews, back-office reroutes.
[01:02] Priya: When you say "per-request metadata", does that include full prompt text? That'd be tricky for us with PII.
[01:08] Ethan: Good question. By default, admin audit entries include metadata — user id, timestamp, action, resource id, request_id, and a small payload field that is truncated. We do not persist full user prompts in admin audit logs unless customers enable additional request capture for debugging. There's also an option for redaction/masking on fields.
[01:32] Daniel: So default stance is conservative — logs won't contain full PII. But if we enable detailed capture for root cause, is there an audit trail that marks that action?
[01:40] Maya: Yes, the action of enabling debug capture itself is an admin event and is logged and retained. That way audits can show who turned on debug and when.
[01:46] Liam: Ok that's good. On retention — what's default retention and can we set longer windows?
[01:53] Ethan: Default retention for admin/audit telemetry in hosted is 90 days. We have configurable retention tiers: 90 (default), 1 year, 3 years behind an enterprise package, or custom retention for Dedicated/Private. We also support legal-hold style exports — you can mark entities and request snapshots for extended archival.
[02:16] Priya: Where do exports land? We run primarily in GCP and AWS. We need to export to our secured buckets.
[02:21] Ethan: Exports can be pushed to S3 or GCS via a secure signed pipeline, or you can opt for streaming webhooks to an on-prem collector. For sensitive setups we provide a push mechanism that encrypts with your KMS key (BYOK) before transit to the bucket. We also do SFTP or HTTPS uploads for customers with specific network constraints.
[02:42] Priya: Is that the same when you run in Dedicated or Private?
[02:46] Ethan: For Dedicated the export endpoints are the same but you can point to VPC-only endpoints. For Private (VPC or on-prem), we give you local export tools that write directly to your storage; keys stay in your KMS/HSM if configured.
[02:58] Daniel: HSM — can you give details? We have on-prem HSMs and strict key custody rules.
[03:03] Maya: Sure. We support two models: 1) Redwood-managed KMS where keys are in Redwood's cloud KMS; 2) BYOK with customer-managed KMS — either cloud KMS (e.g., GCP KMS, AWS KMS) or a customer HSM via KMIP/PKCS11 integration in Private deployments. For the latter, Redwood never stores plaintext keys and we do envelope encryption.
[03:25] Liam: So if we go BYOK with an HSM on-prem, does the audit export pipeline still decrypt/encrypt on Redwood side?
[03:30] Ethan: No — with BYOK/HSM the encryption/decryption lifecycle is under your control. Redwood will sign and encrypt payloads with your public key or wrap with your KEK. We only handle the wrapped blobs. For streaming we can push wrapped blobs directly to your endpoint.
[03:45] Priya: Great. About schema — what fields are in the CSV/JSON payload? We need to align with our SIEM ingestion mapping.
[03:52] Ethan: Sample fields: event_id, timestamp (RFC3339), actor_id (hashed), actor_email (optional), action_type, resource_type, resource_id, ip_address (last octet masked by default), user_agent, request_id, outcome (success/fail), change_summary, retention_flag, legal_hold_id. For debugging payloads there's an optional data field which is truncated or masked. We'll send a sample schema.
[04:20] Priya: Masking for ip_address — you said last octet masked by default? Can we disable masking for internal buckets?
[04:26] Ethan: Yes you can configure masking policies per export target. Default masking is on for hosted. For Dedicated/Private you can choose full IPs if your compliance allows.
[04:33] Daniel: How do you handle cross-region replication? We have EU data residency requirements for some entities.
[04:40] Maya: You can configure residency at the tenant level. Admin telemetry tied to EU-scoped tenants can be stored in EU regions only. For customers with multi-region needs we support geo-tagging and replicated archives, but for regulated entities you can choose to keep logs in region and export to local storage.
[04:58] Liam: Does Redwood provide attestations or connectors for auditors?
[05:02] Maya: Yes — we provide SOC 2 Type II reports and ISO 27001 certificate as part of enterprise package. For private deployments we can run onsite audits and produce evidence packages. We'll include list of available artifacts in the follow-up email.
[05:15] Priya: On the RBAC side — what admin events for SSO do you capture?
[05:19] Ethan: We capture SSO logins, SAML assertion errors, token issuance, token revocations, role assignments, and MFA events. All SSO events are correlated with session IDs and the console events so you can follow a chain from login to admin action.
[05:34] Daniel: Are changes to RBAC config and policy versions immutable in the audit trail? We need non-repudiation for compliance.
[05:40] Ethan: We maintain an immutable append-only store for control-plane events with sequence numbers and checksums. Exports include the sequence numbers so you can verify continuity. For extra assurance we can sign batches with a dedicated signing key.
[05:57] Liam: Signing key — is that Redwood-managed?
[06:00] Maya: Signing keys are Redwood-managed by default, but for Dedicated/Private we can integrate with your signing key or HSM for batch signing.
[06:07] Priya: What about searchability? Our SIEM needs specific fields. Can you index custom fields in the export or add labels?
[06:16] Ethan: Exports include key/value metadata tags you can set per resource. We also support structured JSON exports for direct SIEM ingestion, and a flattened CSV for older pipelines. We'll provide example transform scripts.
[06:29] Daniel: A couple of gotchas from our side: 1) legal holds — we need the ability to freeze deletions for user accounts and related telemetry; 2) we have a requirement to preserve admin trails for at least 7 years for certain products.
[06:44] Maya: Legal holds are supported — you can attach a legal_hold_id to resources and the export pipeline will snapshot and preserve until release. For 7-year retention, that's in the enterprise/private tier — Redwood can commit to that SLA for Dedicated. We'll put the retention options in the follow-up.
[06:58] Liam: For on-prem/private, are there any small-footprint collectors you ship so we don't have to run heavy agents?
[07:04] Ethan: Yes, we have a lightweight collector that streams audit events over TLS to your endpoint. For air-gapped customers we provide a bundle that writes encrypted batches to a mountable disk.
[07:16] Priya: Network-wise, can exports be routed through our proxies? We do strict egress control.
[07:21] Ethan: Yes, our export connectors support proxy endpoints and fixed egress IP ranges for allowlisting. For higher security we recommend Private deployment with inside-the-VPC endpoints.
[07:32] Daniel: Any limitations on event volume or throttling on exports?
[07:36] Ethan: For hosted customers we have rate limits on streaming exports; Dedicated includes higher throughput tiers. If you expect very high volume we recommend batching to S3/GCS or a Dedicated pipe to avoid throttling. We'll capture your expected QPS in the POC planning.
[07:52] Maya: Quick pause — does everyone feel the main items are covered so far?
[07:56] Priya: Yes, but one more: how do you handle deletions requested under data subject requests — do you remove entries from audit trails too?
[08:05] Ethan: We follow data minimization. We can redact PII on request, but we keep an audit stub that indicates an event existed (event_id, timestamp, redaction_marker) so you have non-repudiation without exposing the content. For legal obligations where you must delete everything, we support targeted erasure workflows but this will remove content and create a deletion event in the trail.
[08:28] Daniel: That works. For compliance we'll need the deletion proofs — hash of deleted blob and who authorized.
[08:34] Maya: We can provide deletion receipts including hashed blob IDs and auth chain. We'll add that to artifacts.
[08:41] Liam: Ok, on the topic of formats — you mentioned JSON and CSV, and streaming webhooks. Any timeline on adding parquet or other columnar formats? That would help analytics.
[08:51] Ethan: Parquet export is on our roadmap for Q4 but we can provide a conversion script in the meantime. We'll note that in the POC scope.
[08:59] Priya: One operational detail — does Redwood persist raw request bodies anywhere for a time window? We need to ensure sensitive data isn't lingering.
[09:07] Ethan: By default, raw request bodies for inference are not stored in admin audit logs. For debugging we can enable request capture to a restricted bucket with short TTL and strict access controls, and that action is itself audited.
[09:22] Daniel: Great. Anything about alerting? We want to know if an admin role is granted to a new user, notify secops.
[09:28] Ethan: You can configure webhook alerts for specific admin events like role_grant or key_rotation. Alerts can go to your incident system or to a SIEM.
[09:36] Maya: Ok, let's move toward next steps and recap.
[09:39] Maya: Action items: we'll send artifacts, sample schemas, and scripts; Zenith will provide RBAC mapping and retention constraints; schedule POC planning for next week.
[09:49] Liam: Sounds good. Thanks all.
[09:52] Priya: Thanks.
[09:53] Daniel: Thanks everyone.

(auto-transcribe end)
